Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-06
Start time: 09:15 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Avery (PM), Diego (Eng Lead), Priya (SRE), Samira (QA), Ethan (Infra)
---
Summary (auto): quick incident review after last night's canary. we'll cover what happened, immediate mitigations, and longer term fixes.
Topics (auto): incident timeline, root cause hypotheses, mitigation validation, release gating, action items
Action items (auto): see metadata list
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: okay, good morning everyone, uh let's get started. we spent a fair bit triaging last night so want to go through timeline, root cause, and the rollout plan for next week, um and make sure owners and due dates are clear.
[00:28] Diego: yeah, hi. quick recap from engineering side: around 23:40 UTC last night the canary that was running the 13B-quantized profile started showing increased token latency and a small but measurable drop in quality for a subset of prompts. latency spiked to about 3.8s P95 on the canary region, whereas baseline was 1.6s. we pulled the canary at 00:10 once we confirmed it impacted user-facing paths in staging.
[01:05] Priya: SRE saw the alerts come in, the latency alert threshold was at 2.0s P95 and we hit that. also saw autoscaler not adding nodes fast enough because of cooldown config and GPU provisioning handshake time. so mitigation was to scale up dedicated capacity and roll back the canary to the FP16 variant.
[01:40] Samira: QA noticed that responses from the quantized variant had more hallucinations on our invoice and legal prompts, specifically repeated phrases and some entity hallucination. not all prompts were impacted but the regression was consistent across a seed set.
[02:05] Ethan: infra notes: there was a backlog in our node-provision queue in the region because of a concurrent maintenance job. that increased pod start time by ~90s which meant autoscaler decisions lagged. we had burst capacity configured but it didn't trigger because the nodepool tags were mismatched in the canary policy.
[02:40] Avery: okay so multiple factors: model runtime regression, autoscaler cooldown + nodepool tagging, and a maintenance window interfering. what do we think the primary root cause is — quantization kernel mismatch or infra timing?
[03:10] Diego: initial suspicion is kernel/compilation mismatch for the quantized path. the new kernel selector we shipped had a fallback path that accidentally picked a slower kernel for sequence lengths < 256 due to a heuristic bug. that explains the perf but not necessarily the hallucinations. for quality I think quantization calibration off by a bit — some op ordering changed in a minor optimizer pass.
[03:50] Priya: agreed on mixed causes. from SRE perspective the system should have failed safe: when latency crossed threshold we should have triggered an automatic fallback to the FP16 variant. the fallback didn't execute because the canary routing rules were too permissive — they allowed partial traffic rather than full failover.
[04:20] Samira: also QA coverage missed the particular prompt pattern. our regression harness uses a 100-prompt set but this family of prompts is only in the extended set which wasn't in the canary health checks. so we didn't catch the quality regression in time.
[04:50] Avery: good notes. let's go through timeline in more detail — who has the artifact? Diego?
[05:12] Diego: I pulled logs and saved them to the incident folder, link in the doc: /drive/incidents/2026-12-06-quantized-canary. key entries: 23:37 first minor errors in kernel allocator, 23:40 P95 jump, 23:55 first user reports, 00:03 attempted auto-fallback failed, 00:10 manual rollback to FP16.
[05:45] Priya: adding to that, alert chain: paged at 23:44, on-call escalated to senior SRE at 23:48, we attempted automatic mitigation at 23:59 and it didn't execute due to route mismatch. manual rollback occurred 00:10.
[06:15] Ethan: infra timeline: maintenance job kicked at 23:30 which overlapped, nodepool autoscaler saw capacity at 23:38 but couldn't satisfy because of wrong taints/tolerations on the canary nodepool. that came from a recent IaC change that didn't go through staging.
[06:45] Avery: okay so IaC change + kernel heuristic + incomplete health checks. immediate mitigations you all executed — rollback, increased dedicated pool, follow-up — anything else?
[07:05] Diego: we temporarily disabled the new kernel selector and pinned the quantized model to the previous binary that uses the stable kernel. that reduced latency back to baseline on the canary.
[07:30] Priya: I bumped the alert P95 threshold to 2.5s to reduce noise during triage and updated the playbook to clarify fallback routing.
[07:50] Samira: QA started an extended regression run against the full prompt corpus overnight and we saw the same hallucination cluster. we flagged 12 failing prompts which are attached in the doc.
[08:10] Diego: I also reverted the IaC change in the canary nodepool config to restore the correct tags. Ethan confirmed the nodepool now matches the canary policy.
[08:30] Ethan: yes, nodepool tags fixed, burst capacity exercised in a smoke run, it's behaving now but we need to run dry-run tests for node provisioning in the staging region.
[08:55] Avery: good. let's talk short-term gating for the next rollout: do we require a manual sign-off and dry-run? what's the bar?
[09:20] Diego: propose: require dry-run with autoscaler and maintenance overlap simulation, run the extended QA set, and a canary that's 2% traffic for 24 hours with daily QA checks. plus an automatic fallback check that has to pass in staging.
[09:45] Priya: add: validate fallback routing is operational end-to-end (routing rule tests), and check nodepool tags in plan stage — we can add an IaC preflight check.
[10:05] Samira: from QA: we need the extended prompt corpus in the canary health checks and a small golden set for invoice/legal that must have zero regressions. if any regression, block rollout.
[10:30] Avery: sounds reasonable. what's the ETA to have those gates and checks in place? Diego?
[10:42] Diego: I can get kernel selector revert and pinned binary in by EOD today, but the automated routing test + preflight will take ~2 days. dry-run infra test might take 3 days with scheduling.
[11:00] Ethan: I can run node provisioning dry-runs tomorrow and Friday, shouldn't be more than 48 hours to fully validate. IaC preflight rule we can add as a plan check tomorrow as well.
[11:18] Priya: runbook edits I'll have done by 12/08. I'll also tune alerting and validate automatic fallback in staging.
[11:32] Samira: QA tests, I need to add the 3 failing families to the CI and get passing by 12/12, that includes some model-weighted tolerance thresholds.
[11:50] Avery: okay assign owners: Diego - kernel revert & routing test (due 12/10), Priya - runbook + fallback validation (12/08), Ethan - infra dry-run + IaC preflight (12/11), Samira - QA tests (12/12). I'll draft postmortem (12/09) and coordinate exec summary.
[12:10] Diego: one more technical note — the quantization config we used had a stochastic rounding parameter enabled by default in the new toolchain, which may explain quality variance. we should disable stochastic rounding in quantize pipeline until we validate.
[12:32] Samira: yes that matches the hallucination pattern; stochastic rounding can push logits in a way that breaks some entity alignments.
[12:50] Avery: okay add to the action items: disable stochastic rounding by default in the quantize pipeline until verified.
[13:05] Priya: ops question — do we want to keep the canary policy permissive for now or tighten it to full-fallback?
[13:25] Diego: tighten it. the canary should never permit partial traffic that can't be fully failed-over. fallback path must be tested and enabled by default.
[13:45] Ethan: agree. also recommend we add a smoke test that simulates the maintenance window during our weekly release window planning.
[14:05] Avery: good. any other risks we should note before we close?
[14:20] Samira: risk: downstream customers who use embeddings for compliance checks might see regression — we should notify a small set of internal stakeholders and pause any external canaries until gating is in place.
[14:40] Priya: security note — no PII was exposed or leaked as a result of this incident, but we'll run a quick audit on logs we collected to verify no sensitive prompts were emitted in error paths.
[15:00] Avery: great. last: communications. I'll draft postmortem and an internal note for the eng-all channel, Diego can provide technical appendix and Samira will provide QA findings. we should target sending the note on 12/09 after we've confirmed the revert and initial tests.
[15:30] Diego: also want to capture a short lessons-learned: add IaC preflight checks, extend canary health checks with extended corpus, require fallback test to pass as part of CI.
[15:55] Ethan: and I'll add the nodepool tag validation to our terraform plan checks.
[16:10] Avery: perfect. let's recap next steps quickly: (1) postmortem draft (Avery) by 12/09, (2) kernel revert & routing test (Diego) by 12/10, (3) runbook + fallback validation (Priya) by 12/08, (4) infra dry-run and IaC preflight (Ethan) by 12/11, (5) QA regression tests and CI updates (Samira) by 12/12, (6) disable stochastic rounding in quantize pipeline (Diego) by 12/08.
[17:00] Priya: noted. I'll also run a quick incident retro with the on-call team later today.
[17:20] Samira: I'll pull together the failing prompt examples and include them in the QA appendix.
[17:40] Avery: thanks everyone, if no objections we'll close. I'll follow up with calendar hold for the dry-run and set a check-in on 12/09.
[18:00] Diego: no objections. thanks.
[18:15] Ethan: thanks, bye.
[18:30] (call ends)
